## F01 Loop and built-in tools

- F01.loop-shape — Loop shape [supported, unverified] The agent loop is the repeated reasoning, action and validation steps. When a model requests a tool call, VS Code executes the tool and feeds the result back to the model for the next iteration. Agents self-correct when they encounter errors. A request in progress can be steered, given a queued follow-up, or stopped; stopping does not undo completed actions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00304, E-copilot-vscode-00375, E-copilot-vscode-00257, E-copilot-vscode-00531
- F01.turn-limits — Turn and step limits [supported, verified] The chat.agent.maxRequests setting caps the number of requests the agent can make (listed default 25). Built-in request limits also prevent runaway operations that consume excessive resources or perform unintended bulk actions. For terminal commands, the agent can specify a timeout; when it is reached the agent stops waiting and returns the output collected so far. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00557, E-copilot-vscode-00966, E-copilot-vscode-02706
- F01.tool-inventory — Native tool inventory [supported, unverified] Agents choose from the enabled tools automatically; typing # browses available tools and context items. Tool outputs include file reads, terminal commands and codebase search results. Browser tools (workbench.browser.enableChatTools, default true) let agents interact with integrated-browser pages. Local sessions can use VS Code built-in and extension-provided tools. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00535, E-copilot-vscode-00360, E-copilot-vscode-00553, E-copilot-vscode-00702
- F01.shell-tool — Shell execution tool [supported, unverified] The agent uses one tool to run any terminal command; VS Code evaluates each command separately for approval, and by default commands require explicit approval before they run. Copilot Agent Host sessions use the Copilot SDK built-in shell by default. Setting chat.agentHost.shellTool.initScript.enabled loads ~/.bashrc or PowerShell profiles before each command. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00921, E-copilot-vscode-00752, E-copilot-vscode-00723, E-copilot-vscode-01200
- F01.file-edit-tools — File read, edit and write tools [supported, verified] The Copilot agent harness applies and saves edits directly to the project folder; in Agent Host sessions they have no pending review state, so review the diff before committing. chat.tools.edits.autoApprove uses glob patterns to set which files need approval before edits are applied. A model's optional editTools lists find-replace, multi-find-replace, apply-patch or code-rewrite. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00274, E-copilot-vscode-00959, E-copilot-vscode-00567, E-copilot-vscode-00208
- F01.web-tools — Web search and fetch tools [supported, unverified] Agents can pull in web content with #fetch and use browser tools (workbench.browser.enableChatTools, default true) to interact with pages in the integrated browser. When a tool accesses a URL, such as #web/fetch, approval is separated into two decisions. chat.agent.networkFilter provides network domain filtering for the fetch tool and integrated browser. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01853, E-copilot-vscode-00917, E-copilot-vscode-00424, E-copilot-vscode-00553

## F02 Context and memory

- F02.context-window-size — Context window size [supported, unverified] Different models have different context window sizes. An editor lists available models with their context size, capabilities, billing details and visibility status. A model's optional contextWindow (input plus output, in tokens) lets maxInputTokens be omitted; VS Code derives it as contextWindow minus maxOutputTokens. A chat-input control shows how much of the window the active chat uses. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00376, E-copilot-vscode-00179, E-copilot-vscode-00195, E-copilot-vscode-00982

The setting github.copilot.chat.summarizeAgentConversationHistory.enabled (Experimental, default true) controls it; false turns automatic compaction off. - F04.approval-modes — Approval modes [supported, verified] The session Permissions control sets which actions need your confirmation. Manual permissions requests approval for running tools or accessing resources while the agent can make file edits in the project folder; Allow all is another level. ## F05 Sandbox and network isolation

- F05.os-sandbox — OS or container sandbox [partial, verified] Agent sandboxing uses OS-level isolation to restrict what agent-executed terminal commands can access on your machine; `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled` takes `off` or `on`. On macOS and Linux, locally-running stdio MCP servers can also be sandboxed. An Agent Host session can run in a Dev Container. | limit: It is in Preview on macOS, Linux, and WSL2, and Experimental on Windows. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00970, E-copilot-vscode-00578, E-copilot-vscode-00214, E-copilot-vscode-00786
- F05.fs-write-scope — Filesystem write scope [partial, verified] Built-in agent tools can only read and write files within the current workspace folder, with optional read-only access to additional folders via `chat.additionalReadAccessFolders`. Sandbox file system isolation limits read and write access to configured paths. A Git worktree is a code-isolation boundary, not a security boundary. | limit: Sandboxing does not restrict built-in file tools or replace approval controls for other tools. A worktree does not restrict commands, network access, or access to files outside the worktree. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00965, E-copilot-vscode-00416, E-copilot-vscode-01146, E-copilot-vscode-00302
- F05.network-policy — Network policy [partial, verified] `chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork` (Preview) permits unrestricted network access while preserving file system restrictions; when `false`, the Copilot Agent Host built-in shell and Windows terminal sandbox block outbound access. Sandboxed MCP servers can only access network domains you explicitly permit. | limit: On macOS and Linux, you can enable sandboxing for locally-running stdio MCP servers to restrict their access to the file system and network. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00580, E-copilot-vscode-00214, E-copilot-vscode-01044
- F05.subprocess-containment — Subprocess containment [supported, verified] Sandboxing applies to terminal commands and their child processes, not to built-in file tools or other agent tools. Both boundaries are applied at the operating system level and inherited by child processes, which cannot bypass them; file system restrictions apply equally to child processes such as build scripts and package managers. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00419, E-copilot-vscode-00420, E-copilot-vscode-00747, E-copilot-vscode-00756
- F05.sandbox-override — Sandbox override [supported, unverified] If a command cannot run inside the sandbox, the agent can ask for confirmation to run it outside; `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` (Preview) controls this for Local and Copilot Agent Host sessions. When `false`, Allow Outside Sandbox is not offered and such requests fail. `sandbox.allowBypass` set `false` from any channel takes precedence over `true` from another. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00767, E-copilot-vscode-00581, E-copilot-vscode-00768, E-copilot-vscode-01044

## F07 Managed and enterprise controls

- F07.managed-settings — Managed settings delivery [supported, unverified] Copilot managed settings are a centrally-managed governance layer that applies the same configuration across VS Code and GitHub Copilot CLI. Most managed settings map to a VS Code enterprise policy and override the corresponding user setting on managed devices. Organization administrators can manage Copilot through enterprise AI settings and policies. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01035, E-copilot-vscode-00333
- F07.policy-lockdown — Policy lockdown [supported, unverified] The `ChatAgentMode` policy (setting `chat.agent.enabled`) prevents the use of agent mode entirely. Organizations can use device management policies to enforce manual approvals for specific tools, and can enforce network restrictions that you cannot relax with a local setting. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00976, E-copilot-vscode-01168, E-copilot-vscode-00915, E-copilot-vscode-00765
- F07.model-allowlist — Model allow and deny lists [supported, unverified] Organizations can restrict access to certain models. Auto won't select models excluded by administrator policies or restricted by data-residency policies. The `ChatDefaultModel` policy sets the default chat model for new conversations; users can still switch the model within a conversation. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00263, E-copilot-vscode-00387, E-copilot-vscode-01178
- F07.identity-sso — Identity and SSO [supported, verified] Copilot sessions reuse VS Code chat's GitHub authentication context. A policy set to a non-empty list disables all AI features until the user signs into a GitHub account whose organizations intersect it and account-side policy data has resolved. (Preview) `enterpriseManaged` authenticates via the enterprise SSO issuer set by `mcp.enterpriseManagedAuth.idp` (ID-JAG). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01177, E-copilot-vscode-00624, E-copilot-vscode-00801
- F07.data-retention — Data retention and privacy [supported, verified] The model configuration option `zeroDataRetentionEnabled` (default `false`) is set to `true` if Zero Data Retention (ZDR) is enabled for the endpoint; then `previous_response_id` is not sent in Responses API requests. By default, no prompt content, responses, or tool arguments are captured. Setting `chat.sessionSync.enabled` to `false` keeps session data local only. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00209, E-copilot-vscode-00485, E-copilot-vscode-02659
- F07.admin-audit — Admin audit and reporting [partial, verified] The Developer: Policy Diagnostics command opens an untitled Markdown report of the current policy state on the device, showing the effective policy value and its source. For Local harness sessions, identity capture can attribute agent activity to an individual developer and machine. | limit: Identity capture is described 'For Local harness sessions'. On the session-history page, 'Enabling the policy does not give administrators access to your session data.' | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01052, E-copilot-vscode-02899, E-copilot-vscode-00483, E-copilot-vscode-02665

## F08 Skills

- F08.skill-format — Skill format [supported, verified] A skill is a `SKILL.md` Markdown file with YAML frontmatter that defines its metadata and behavior. The required `name` allows only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, must match the parent directory name, and is at most 64 characters; a plugin skill name must be plain kebab-case without namespace prefixes, or the skill is silently skipped. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00100, E-copilot-vscode-00101, E-copilot-vscode-01525
- F08.discovery-paths — Discovery paths [partial, verified] Example workspace skill path: `.github/skills/validate-change/SKILL.md`. The Agent Host reads user-level customizations from folders like `~/.copilot` and `~/.claude`. `chat.agentSkillsLocations` configures additional locations for the Local agent. The Load Skills event detail lists the paths searched, in order, and which skills were found and loaded. | limit: The location settings are deprecated because Agent Host sessions don't use them; customizations stored only in VS Code profile user data are a legacy location that the Copilot agent doesn't read. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02045, E-copilot-vscode-01908, E-copilot-vscode-01742, E-copilot-vscode-03024
- F08.invocation — Invocation [supported, unverified] The agent loads a skill when the task matches, or you invoke it directly. Typing `/` in the chat input and selecting the skill invokes it explicitly, and `/‹name›` invokes an agent skill or reusable prompt by name. The `description` field states what the skill does and when to use it, to help Copilot decide when to load the skill. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01943, E-copilot-vscode-02049, E-copilot-vscode-00103, E-copilot-vscode-00541
- F08.resource-loading — Resource loading [supported, unverified] Copilot accesses additional files in the skill directory only when the instructions reference them; an unreferenced file is not loaded. A skill can include instructions, scripts, templates, examples, and other resources that the agent loads when relevant. By default, a loaded skill's instructions are added to the parent agent's context window. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01557, E-copilot-vscode-02044, E-copilot-vscode-00113
- F08.skill-overrides — Per-skill tool and model overrides [undocumented, verified] swept for: skills?\b.{0,100}(allowed-tools|model|effort|frontmatter); allowed-tools; hits 13, reviewed 13; positive control `copilot`: 1055 hits

## F09 Subagents and custom agents

- F09.definition-format — Definition format [partial, verified] Custom agent files use the `.agent.md` extension, with an optional YAML header that configures the agent and a Markdown body that provides its instructions. The `tools` metadata field sets the available tools, and `hooks` in `.agent.md` frontmatter scope hooks to that agent. Example workspace agent: `.github/agents/researcher.agent.md`. | limit: `hooks` in `.agent.md` frontmatter 'Runs only for that custom agent in the Local harness.' | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00116, E-copilot-vscode-02052, E-copilot-vscode-01764, E-copilot-vscode-00152
- F09.tool-allowlist — Tool allow-list [supported, unverified] A custom agent's available tools are set with the `tools` metadata field, which prompt files also use. The field can include built-in tools, tool sets, MCP tools, or tools contributed by extensions, and `‹server name›/*` includes all tools of an MCP server. A tool set is a reusable collection of tools referenced as a single entity in custom agents. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00120, E-copilot-vscode-01764, E-copilot-vscode-01773
- F09.per-agent-model — Per-agent model [supported, verified] A custom agent's model property takes a single model name or a prioritized list, tried in order until an available one is found; if unset, the currently selected model is used. A custom agent run as a subagent can override the tools and model. Preferred models can be pinned in prompt files or custom agent definitions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00125, E-copilot-vscode-01007, E-copilot-vscode-00280
- F09.per-agent-effort — Per-agent effort [undocumented, verified] swept for: (sub-?agents?|custom agents?|agent definitions?|per-agent|each agent).{0,100}(effort|reasoning|thinking); (effort|reasoning|thinking).{0,100}(sub-?agents?|per-agent|custom agents?); hits 0, reviewed 0; positive control `copilot`: 1055 hits
- F09.nesting-rules — Nesting rules [supported, verified] chat.subagents.allowInvocationsFromSubagents (default false) lets subagents invoke other subagents, up to a maximum nesting depth of five. A custom agent's agents field lists permitted subagents (* for all, [] to prevent any subagent use). chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits sets process-wide limits on recursive session creation. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00558, E-copilot-vscode-00122, E-copilot-vscode-01010, E-copilot-vscode-02648
- F09.built-in-agents — Built-in agent types [supported, unverified] A built-in Plan agent researches the codebase, clarifies requirements, and proposes an implementation plan before code changes begin. Rubber Duck is a built-in, read-only critic that gives Copilot a second opinion on its plans, code, and tests. A built-in research agent produces thorough, well-cited reports. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00305, E-copilot-vscode-00725, E-copilot-vscode-00428

## F10 Slash and custom commands

- F10.built-in-commands — Built-in commands [supported, unverified] Chat has built-in slash commands, for example `/plan` (research and propose an implementation plan) and `/compact` (compact the conversation manually). Entering `/` in the chat input of a Copilot session lists the slash commands available there; `/yolo` and `/autoApprove` are given as examples for controlling automatic tool approval. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00536, E-copilot-vscode-00724, E-copilot-vscode-00364
- F10.custom-command-format — Custom command format [partial, verified] Prompt files are Markdown files with the `.prompt.md` extension; an optional YAML frontmatter header configures the prompt's behavior. A prompt file can add the `agent` tool set to its `tools` frontmatter to delegate to subagents, and one documented example path is `.github/prompts/plan.prompt.md`. | limit: Prompt files are deprecated for Agent Host sessions and aren't loaded by Agent Host. They continue to work with the Local agent for now, but the Local agent will be removed in a future release. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00218, E-copilot-vscode-01006, E-copilot-vscode-00434, E-copilot-vscode-01739
- F10.arguments — Arguments [supported, verified] Extra text can follow a slash command in the chat input: `/create-react-form formName=MyForm` or `/create-api for listing customers` for prompt files, and `/webapp-testing for the login page` for skills. `/compact` accepts optional custom instructions after the command; in the Agents window, `/troubleshoot #session` selects a local or remote session before you add your question. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01760, E-copilot-vscode-01551, E-copilot-vscode-00379, E-copilot-vscode-00243
- F10.discovery-paths — Discovery paths [partial, verified] Prompt files can be stored in a workspace or at user level, where they are available across all workspaces; workspace prompt files apply only to that workspace. In a monorepo, enabling `chat.useCustomizationsInParentRepositories` discovers prompt files from the parent repository root. The Local agent has default file locations for each scope. | limit: The documented locations are those the Local agent uses; `chat.promptFilesLocations` (Deprecated) configures prompt file locations for the Local agent, and this setting and the Local agent will be removed in a future release. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01750, E-copilot-vscode-01754, E-copilot-vscode-01753, E-copilot-vscode-02283
- F10.command-skill-relation — Relation to skills [supported, unverified] Skills and prompt files both appear as slash commands in chat, alongside each other: typing `/` lists them, and `/‹name›` invokes an agent skill or reusable prompt by name. Prompt files are also known as slash commands, and Migrate Prompt Files converts workspace and user prompt files to agent skills. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00541, E-copilot-vscode-01550, E-copilot-vscode-01747, E-copilot-vscode-01736

## F11 Plugins and marketplaces

- F11.packaging-format — Packaging format [supported, unverified] An Agent Plugins 1.0 package has a `plugin.json` file at its root that declares the standard's schema; `$schema` is a required string holding the canonical Agent Plugins schema identifier. The existing Copilot and Claude plugin formats keep their own layouts. For extensions, a chat participant is defined in the extension's `package.json`. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01452, E-copilot-vscode-01453, E-copilot-vscode-01442, E-copilot-vscode-00009
- F11.component-types — Component types [supported, unverified] Agent plugins install multiple related customization types as one package and can bundle MCP servers. A skill distributed through a plugin gets the plugin name as an automatic command prefix (for example, `/my-plugin:test-runner`). In an Agent Plugins package, most client-specific capabilities such as rules, hooks and automation templates come from the `com.github.copilot` namespace. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00372, E-copilot-vscode-01717, E-copilot-vscode-00108, E-copilot-vscode-01442
- F11.install-sources — Install sources [supported, unverified] Plugins are discovered and installed from plugin marketplaces in VS Code, and from the Customizations editor. The `ChatExtraMarketplaces` policy adds marketplaces keyed by name, with values as GitHub shorthand (`owner/repo[#ref]`) or Git URIs. `chat.pluginLocations` (Experimental) registers locally cloned or downloaded plugins by mapping directory paths to enabled or disabled. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01440, E-copilot-vscode-01182, E-copilot-vscode-02303, E-copilot-vscode-01726
- F11.versioning-update — Versioning and update [partial, verified] VS Code checks for plugin updates when you run Extensions: Check for Extension Updates, or every 24 hours when `extensions.autoUpdate` is enabled. The `plugin.json` `version` field is optional and Semantic Versioning is recommended. Managed `extraKnownMarketplaces` can add marketplaces with optional per-marketplace automatic updates. | limit: Plugins sourced from npm or PyPI never update automatically. Instead, they show an Update button in the Extensions view. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01513, E-copilot-vscode-01454, E-copilot-vscode-01515, E-copilot-vscode-01252
- F11.trust-signing — Trust and signing [partial, verified] The first install from a new marketplace shows a trust prompt to review the marketplace source. `ChatStrictMarketplaces` is an allowlist of plugin marketplace sources: only matching marketplaces are trusted, and an empty array blocks all. Docs advise reviewing plugin contents and publisher before installing, since plugins can include hooks and MCP servers that run code on your machine. | limit: `strictKnownMarketplaces` restricts plugin installation to the listed sources. It does not retroactively disable already-installed plugins. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01499, E-copilot-vscode-01183, E-copilot-vscode-02832, E-copilot-vscode-01451
- F11.marketplace-hosting — Marketplace hosting [supported, verified] Additional plugin marketplaces are Git repositories configured through the `chat.plugins.marketplaces` setting (Experimental). The `ChatExtraMarketplaces` policy takes GitHub shorthand (`owner/repo[#ref]`) or Git URIs, optionally with an enterprise-managed auto-update override. A plugin, such as one packaging reviewed hook scripts, can be published in your approved marketplace. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02300, E-copilot-vscode-01182, E-copilot-vscode-02827, E-copilot-vscode-01506

## F12 MCP

- F12.client-support — Client support [supported, verified] VS Code supports MCP tools to integrate external services with language models; in VS Code, MCP servers expose their capabilities as tools. MCP prompts are supported as reusable prompts added as slash commands in chat. The Local harness can use MCP servers. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00004, E-copilot-vscode-00053, E-copilot-vscode-01670, E-copilot-vscode-00713
- F12.transports — Transports [supported, unverified] Standard I/O (stdio) servers are the most common type for locally-run MCP servers. For HTTP servers VS Code first tries the HTTP Stream transport and falls back to SSE; SSE has legacy support. HTTP servers can also listen on Unix sockets (`unix:///path/to/server.sock`) or Windows named pipes (`pipe:///pipe/named-pipe`). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00621, E-copilot-vscode-00622, E-copilot-vscode-00052, E-copilot-vscode-00623
- F12.config-scope — Config location and scope [partial, verified] VS Code-format MCP config is `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace or the user profile, with a top-level `servers` object. The Agent Host reads harness-agnostic config from `.mcp.json` (workspace) and `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` (user); servers can be migrated to workspace `.mcp.json` or user `$COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json`. | limit: The Agent Host doesn't read `.vscode/mcp.json` directly, but VS Code forwards servers you configure in VS Code to the Agent Host, except servers that require interactive... | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00615, E-copilot-vscode-01913, E-copilot-vscode-01737
- F12.auth — Authentication [partial, verified] VS Code supports MCP authentication, authorizing access to an MCP server using OAuth. HTTP and SSE servers accept a `headers` field for authentication or configuration headers. The `McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp` policy supplies the OAuth/OIDC IdP configuration for enterprise-managed MCP server authentication. | limit: Copilot sessions can currently access only local MCP servers that don't require authentication. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00057, E-copilot-vscode-00691, E-copilot-vscode-01188, E-copilot-vscode-00729
- F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming [supported, unverified] Configure Tools in the chat input lists an MCP server's tools and lets you toggle specific tools on or off; MCP tools can be enabled and configured with the tools picker. A custom agent's `tools` field can include all tools of an MCP server with `‹server name›/*`. An experimental setting groups tools into virtual tools activated on demand, to go beyond the limit of 128 tools for a chat request. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01675, E-copilot-vscode-00120, E-copilot-vscode-00593, E-copilot-vscode-00059
- F12.server-trust — Server trust and approval [partial, verified] MCP tool invocations require explicit user approval, grantable at session, workspace or user level. VS Code uses trust decisions for MCP servers, and workspace MCP servers inherit Workspace Trust. The ChatMCP policy (setting chat.mcp.access) controls access to installed MCP servers. | limit: Plugin MCP servers are implicitly trusted when you install the plugin. Unlike workspace MCP servers, they do not show a separate trust prompt at startup. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00968, E-copilot-vscode-00409, E-copilot-vscode-01180, E-copilot-vscode-01482

## F13 Sessions, checkpoints, rewind

- F13.resume-continue — Resume and continue [supported, verified] Reloading the window and reopening a session restores visible and hidden chats with their conversation history. A session from another application can be continued in VS Code by opening it and sending a message. An existing Copilot session can be continued in the terminal via Resume in Terminal. Archived sessions can be searched for and reopened. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00990, E-copilot-vscode-01808, E-copilot-vscode-00728, E-copilot-vscode-02978
- F13.fork-branch — Fork or branch a session [partial, verified] /fork branches the conversation with its history. Hovering over a request and selecting Fork Conversation creates an independent session that includes the conversation up to that checkpoint. A fork inherits the source conversation up to the fork point, and the original conversation remains available. | limit: Forking doesn't guarantee separate code changes; a fork can share the original session and worktree (E-copilot-vscode-00396), whereas E-copilot-vscode-02592 describes the fork as an independent session. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02434, E-copilot-vscode-00396, E-copilot-vscode-02592, E-copilot-vscode-00537
- F13.checkpoint-rewind — Checkpoint and rewind [partial, verified] Hovering over an earlier request and selecting Restore Checkpoint restores affected workspace files and chat history. For supported sessions, checkpoints restore affected workspace files and chat to an earlier point. The setting chat.checkpoints.enabled enables or disables checkpoints in the chat. | limit: It doesn't reverse terminal commands, network requests, deployments, or changes to external services. Described for supported sessions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02223, E-copilot-vscode-00404, E-copilot-vscode-00545, E-copilot-vscode-01849
- F13.transcript-storage — Transcript storage [partial, verified] VS Code maintains a searchable history of Copilot sessions and by default syncs local agent sessions to the user's GitHub account. When session sync is disabled by organization policy, session data is kept local only. Hook input can carry an optional absolute path to a file that contains the conversation transcript. | limit: Transcript formats are not a stable cross-harness API. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02657, E-copilot-vscode-01184, E-copilot-vscode-02324, E-copilot-vscode-01654
- F13.session-listing — Session naming and listing [supported, unverified] The Agents window sidebar lists active agent sessions, grouped by workspace, for switching between them. A setting controls which sessions from supported external applications appear in the session lists (none, recent, last24Hours, last7Days, all). In an Agent Host session, each chat has its own conversation history and title. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00268, E-copilot-vscode-00594, E-copilot-vscode-00986
- F13.cross-surface-handoff — Cross-surface handoff [supported, unverified] Changing the session target hands a session off while preserving the conversation history and context. A session from another application can be continued in VS Code by opening it and sending a message. An existing Copilot session can be continued in a terminal via Resume in Terminal. In the Agents window, Open in Editor opens the session's workspace in an editor window. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01866, E-copilot-vscode-01808, E-copilot-vscode-00991, E-copilot-vscode-00728

## F14 Worktrees and parallel execution

- F14.worktree-isolation — Worktree isolation [partial, verified] The Code isolation control sets whether changes go into the current folder or a separate Git worktree. Separate sessions, each with a new worktree, give each task its own working files and branch; integration can still produce conflicts. A Git worktree separates code changes. | limit: A Git worktree separates code changes, but is not a security boundary. For the Copilot harness, worktree sessions always use Allow all. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00628, E-copilot-vscode-00438, E-copilot-vscode-00899, E-copilot-vscode-00533
- F14.concurrency-caps — Concurrency caps [partial, verified] An automation runs one session at a time and another scheduled occurrence does not start a parallel run of the same automation. chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits (Experimental) sets process-wide limits on sessions and chats created, messages sent and recursive session creation by Agent Host session tools. Burst sends are capped to avoid unbounded fan-out. | limit: An automation runs one session at a time. Orchestration limits apply to Agent Host session tools, and no numeric limit is quoted. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00606, E-copilot-vscode-02511, E-copilot-vscode-02647
- F14.parallel-subagents — Parallel subagents [partial, verified] Independent subtasks can run in parallel, such as separate correctness and performance reviews. The user can also ask the AI to run multiple independent tasks in parallel. | limit: Independent subtasks can run in parallel when the harness supports concurrent subagents. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00308, E-copilot-vscode-01851
- F14.total-agent-caps — Total agent caps [partial, verified] chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits (Experimental) sets process-wide limits on sessions and chats created, messages sent and recursive session creation by Agent Host session tools; the default on value enforces limits and off removes them. Burst sends are capped. Local subagents cannot invoke further subagents by default; nesting is limited to a maximum depth of five. | limit: Limits apply to sessions and chats created, messages sent and recursive session creation by Agent Host session tools; no numeric total is quoted. Set it to off to remove the limits. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00606, E-copilot-vscode-01020, E-copilot-vscode-02647, E-copilot-vscode-02649
- F14.multi-session-coordination — Multi-session coordination [partial, verified] Sessions are independent, can run in parallel, and are shared across the Chat view and the Agents window. Separate sessions using the same folder have separate conversations. Separate tools coordinate work across Agent Host sessions (session orchestration). | limit: For separate sessions using the same folder: conversations are separate, but both sessions can edit the same working files. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01924, E-copilot-vscode-00437, E-copilot-vscode-02383

## F15 Background, scheduled and cloud-delegated work

- F15.background-tasks — Background tasks [supported, verified] A long-running terminal command can be pushed to the background so the agent continues with other tasks. Background sessions run locally and isolated from the main context; Alt+Enter, or holding Alt and selecting Send, starts a new session in the background, and starting a new session leaves the previous one working in the background. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02704, E-copilot-vscode-00284, E-copilot-vscode-00784, E-copilot-vscode-02976
- F15.scheduled-routines — Scheduled routines [partial, verified] Automations run agent tasks from a saved prompt, session configuration, and schedule. A task can run on demand or be scheduled hourly, daily, or weekly. Enable the setting chat.automations.enabled, then select Automations in the sidebar. | limit: chat.automations.enabled is listed as true on Insiders and false on Stable. When disabled, automation entry points are hidden and scheduled tasks aren't dispatched. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02479, E-copilot-vscode-00597, E-copilot-vscode-02501
- F15.cloud-agents — Cloud agents [partial, verified] The Cloud session target runs a well-scoped task independently against a GitHub repository and returns a pull request. A task can be handed off to the Cloud target for remote execution and a pull request workflow. Cloud agents are started by choosing the Cloud session target and a repository. | limit: Copilot Cloud sessions are only supported for GitHub-backed repositories. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00632, E-copilot-vscode-02481, E-copilot-vscode-01968, E-copilot-vscode-02233
- F15.remote-sessions — Remote sessions [supported, verified] Setting github.copilot.chat.cli.remote.enabled enables remote control of Copilot sessions from github.com or the GitHub Mobile app. Multiple clients can observe and control the same Agent Host session, staying in sync. The Agents window can be used in a browser from any device. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00598, E-copilot-vscode-01885, E-copilot-vscode-00777
- F15.event-triggers — Event triggers [supported, unverified] Sessions that you create by assigning an issue or pull request to a cloud agent on GitHub.com also appear in VS Code. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00830
- F15.delegation — Delegation to other agents [partial, verified] In a Copilot session, /delegate continues the task in the cloud. A Continue in dropdown next to Start Implementation hands a plan to an available destination. An Agent Host session can delegate a task to a connected remote host. Custom agents can define handoffs, suggested next actions to transition between custom agents. | limit: The Continue in dropdown appears only when supported destinations are available. Remote delegation requires enabling chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled and chat.remoteSessions.tools.enabled and connecting hosts. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00745, E-copilot-vscode-00947, E-copilot-vscode-00952, E-copilot-vscode-00133

## F17 Model selection and routing

- F17.model-picker — Model picker [supported, verified] The language model picker in the chat input field changes the model for chat conversations and code editing. Users can choose which models are available in the picker. Its hover menu shows cost per token type and a generic cost tier label (Low, Medium, High). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00165, E-copilot-vscode-00262, E-copilot-vscode-00490
- F17.model-flag-env — Flag, setting and environment [supported, verified] The chat.defaultModel setting (enterprise policy, from 1.127) sets the default chat model for new conversations; chat.planAgent.defaultModel sets the Local planning model; inlineChat.defaultModel sets the inline chat model. A prompt file's model field sets its model, and the picker's selection is used if unset. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01178, E-copilot-vscode-00949, E-copilot-vscode-01033, E-copilot-vscode-00222
- F17.auto-routing — Automatic routing [supported, verified] Auto model selection evaluates task complexity and real-time model availability to route each request to the optimal model, combining a model health and availability system with a task-complexity system. chat.subagents.defaultToAuto (default false) makes subagents use Auto when no model is specified; the autoTier managed setting chooses how new chats initially optimize routing. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00175, E-copilot-vscode-00385, E-copilot-vscode-01018, E-copilot-vscode-01056
- F17.provider-byok — Providers and bring-your-own-key [partial, verified] Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) connects any compatible model provider, to access models from other providers, run models locally, or use models not yet built in, while keeping the VS Code chat experience and tools. Instead of the Copilot harness, a user can pick Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex, or a model with their own API key. | limit: Some features, including inline suggestions, semantic search, and embeddings, require the GitHub Copilot service and aren't available through bring-your-own-key models. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00182, E-copilot-vscode-00503, E-copilot-vscode-00511, E-copilot-vscode-00249
- F17.model-catalog — Model catalog and availability [partial, verified] The language models editor shows all available models, lets you choose which are shown in the model picker, and adds models from built-in or extension-provided providers. ## F18 Reasoning effort and thinking

- F18.effort-values — Effort values and defaults [partial, verified] The introduction guide describes Low (less reasoning, faster responses), Medium (balanced reasoning and speed) and High (maximum reasoning depth). Some models also support adaptive thinking, where the model dynamically decides whether and how much to reason. | limit: The available effort levels and their default values vary by model and provider. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00381, E-copilot-vscode-01226, E-copilot-vscode-01336, E-copilot-vscode-01227
- F18.where-set — Where effort is set [supported, verified] Thinking effort is set from the language model picker: select the › arrow next to the model name to open the Thinking Effort submenu. The github.copilot.chat.anthropic.thinking.effort and github.copilot.chat.responsesApiReasoningEffort settings are deprecated; configure thinking effort directly from the picker. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00171, E-copilot-vscode-00281, E-copilot-vscode-00174, E-copilot-vscode-01328
- F18.model-dependence — Model dependence [supported, verified] Available effort levels and defaults vary by model and provider. Non-reasoning models, such as GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o, do not show the thinking effort submenu. The supportsReasoningEffort model property lists the levels a model accepts; when set, a Thinking Effort picker is shown. Capabilities such as thinking are model-dependent and might differ from the built-in models. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00381, E-copilot-vscode-00172, E-copilot-vscode-00210, E-copilot-vscode-00456
- F18.thinking-budget-visibility — Thinking budget and visibility [partial, verified] Higher thinking effort produces more thinking tokens, which increases AI credit consumption. Thinking tokens count toward the context window though not visible in the response; the output is typically returned in summarized form or can be omitted. The experimental chat.agent.thinkingStyle setting configures how thinking is rendered in chat. | limit: The actual thinking output is typically returned in summarized form or can be omitted entirely for lower latency. chat.agent.thinkingStyle is marked (Experimental). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00170, E-copilot-vscode-00383, E-copilot-vscode-00649

## F19 Modes and autonomy levels

- F19.named-modes — Named modes [supported, verified] Agent roles set which instructions, tools, and behavior apply to a task; examples include Agent, Plan, Ask, and custom agents. Agent is for implementation and Plan is to review an approach first; Ask is for questions when the selected target provides it. A prompt file's agent field accepts ask, agent, plan, or a custom agent name. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00291, E-copilot-vscode-00699, E-copilot-vscode-00221
- F19.entering-modes — How modes are entered [supported, verified] Roles can be switched during a session from the agent picker. /plan switches the session to Plan mode and submits the request; Plan can also be selected from the agent mode picker. Autopilot is selected from the mode picker in the chat input. Experimental github.copilot.chat.switchAgent.enabled lets Agent choose to switch to Plan. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00800, E-copilot-vscode-00936, E-copilot-vscode-00906, E-copilot-vscode-00951
- F19.plan-mode — Plan mode [supported, verified] The built-in Plan agent researches the codebase, clarifies requirements and proposes an implementation plan before code changes begin; Plan mode outlines what it would do and waits for approval before acting. The reviewed plan can then be handed off to an implementation agent. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00305, E-copilot-vscode-01222, E-copilot-vscode-01967
- F19.autonomy-mode — Auto-accept and autonomous modes [supported, verified] Autopilot is an agent mode, chosen from the mode picker in the chat input, in which the agent works autonomously until it determines the task is complete. Global auto approve (YOLO mode) disables manual approval for all tools in all workspaces. Bypass Approvals auto-approves all tool calls and retries on errors. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00906, E-copilot-vscode-01186, E-copilot-vscode-01207
- F19.read-only-mode — Read-only or ask mode [supported, verified] Ask mode is back-and-forth conversation with no edits and no commands. The built-in Ask role asks questions and provides guidance without making changes to the code. The Plan agent uses read-only tools while preparing the plan. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01221, E-copilot-vscode-00714, E-copilot-vscode-00306
- F19.mode-defaults — Mode defaults and persistence [partial, verified] New sessions use the permission level set by chat.permissions.default, which offers Manual, Allow all or Autopilot, and the level can be changed per session. Default approvals is the default mode: Copilot follows configured settings and shows confirmation dialogs where required. | limit: If enterprise policy disables auto-approval, new sessions use Manual permissions. On the Agent Host, Autopilot is selected as an agent mode instead. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00898, E-copilot-vscode-01206, E-copilot-vscode-00571

## F20 Version, release channel, update path

- F20.version-at-retrieval — Version at retrieval [supported, verified] The VS Code release notes page describes Visual Studio Code 1.140. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-90002
- F20.release-channels — Release channels [supported, verified] The Copilot extensions have a pre-release (nightly) version, selectable from the Extensions view with Switch to Pre-Release Version. Defaults differ between Stable and Insiders: the Automations setting is off by default on Stable and on by default in Insiders, and persistent progress defaults to Draw in Insiders and Off in Stable. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01804, E-copilot-vscode-02502, E-copilot-vscode-02750
- F20.update-mechanism — Update mechanism [supported, unverified] VS Code can receive automatic updates, fetched from a Microsoft online service, configured by the UpdateMode policy (update.mode). Code: Check for Updates updates VS Code. If built-in updates are disabled by policy, the minimum-version notice directs the developer to contact an administrator. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01261, E-copilot-vscode-00332, E-copilot-vscode-02816
- F20.changelog-source — Changelog source [supported, verified] Release notes for previous VS Code versions are on the Updates page at code.visualstudio.com, as the 1.140 release notes page says. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-90001
- F20.deprecation-policy — Deprecation policy [supported, unverified] Deprecations are noted inline in the docs: infer is deprecated in favour of user-invocable and disable-model-invocation; github.copilot.chat.customOAIModels is marked (Deprecated) in the settings reference. Prompt files are deprecated for Agent Host sessions, and the Local agent will be removed in a future release. Legacy copilot_chat.* telemetry keys have no sunset date. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00130, E-copilot-vscode-01739, E-copilot-vscode-00549, E-copilot-vscode-00477

## F21 Relationship to host platform

- F21.host-platform — Host platform [supported, verified] Runs in VS Code, where the GitHub Copilot Chat panel is the harness. The Local harness runs interactively in the VS Code extension host in the active workspace; the Agent Host runs the harness and owns sessions, while the Chat view and Agents window display and control them. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01218, E-copilot-vscode-00799, E-copilot-vscode-00294
- F21.shared-account-billing — Shared account and billing [partial, verified] Requests in the quickstart use AI credits from your Copilot plan, and Copilot Free includes a monthly allowance. Claude Agent sessions use your existing Copilot subscription. The Agents window uses the AI providers and accounts configured in VS Code and shares settings and the default profile with the main VS Code window. | limit: BYOK models work without signing into a GitHub account and without a Copilot plan. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00512, E-copilot-vscode-02864, E-copilot-vscode-02441, E-copilot-vscode-00183
- F21.shared-execution-infrastructure — Shared execution infrastructure [supported, verified] Provider harnesses (Copilot, Claude, Codex) execute on your machine, a connected host, or a Dev Container, depending on the host and available harness. The Agent Host can run on your machine, inside a Dev Container, or on a remote machine, and file edits and commands run in the environment that contains the host. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01880, E-copilot-vscode-01895
- F21.shared-model-selection — Shared model selection [supported, verified] Model and harness are independent choices: changing the model within a harness does not switch harnesses or convert project customizations, and a Claude model in a Copilot session still uses the Copilot harness. Where tools run and where the model is hosted are separate choices. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00630, E-copilot-vscode-02028, E-copilot-vscode-00509
- F21.shared-agent-runtime — Shared agent runtime [partial, verified] The harness is the software layer that coordinates the agent loop. The Copilot session target runs the session through the Copilot agent harness using the GitHub Copilot SDK; Claude agent sessions are powered by Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK. The experimental chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness setting selects the Copilot SDK harness over Local for new editor-chat sessions. | limit: Enable chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness (Experimental) to use the Copilot SDK harness when Local would otherwise be selected for a new editor-chat session. It does not migrate existing sessions. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00270, E-copilot-vscode-00287, E-copilot-vscode-00590, E-copilot-vscode-00717
- F21.delegates-to — Delegates to [supported, verified] VS Code supports multiple agent harnesses, including Copilot, Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex, managed through a shared VS Code session experience. Claude and Codex session targets keep that provider's agent workflow inside VS Code. A Copilot session can be continued in the terminal with GitHub Copilot CLI via Resume in Terminal. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00288, E-copilot-vscode-00631, E-copilot-vscode-01811
- F21.distinct-harness-features — Distinct harness features [partial, verified] The chosen harness determines how subagents run and which configuration options they support. The Local and Copilot harnesses use different controls to select client-side tools. BYOK models in Agent Host sessions need chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled turned on. | limit: These events, settings, payloads, and output decisions do not automatically apply to Copilot, Claude, or Codex sessions on Agent Host (said of the Local hook implementation). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01094, E-copilot-vscode-01030, E-copilot-vscode-00184, E-copilot-vscode-00148

## F22 Usage, cost, limits and observability

- F22.usage-visibility — Usage and cost visibility [supported, unverified] The context window control in the chat input shows the token count, a usage breakdown, and total AI credits consumed by the session. The Copilot status dashboard in the VS Code Status Bar shows current usage. The model picker hover shows cost per token type and a cost tier label (Low, Medium, High). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00982, E-copilot-vscode-00251, E-copilot-vscode-00490
- F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps [partial, verified] Paid plans include a monthly AI credits allowance. Once AI credits are exhausted, a user can set a budget for additional usage and keep working, or wait until the next monthly cycle when the allowance resets. | limit: If you're on a paid plan and exhaust your AI credits, you can set a budget for additional usage | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00254, E-copilot-vscode-00261
- F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour [supported, unverified] A temporary rate limit can occur even when the monthly AI credits allowance is not exhausted; wait a few minutes and retry. The inline suggestions and AI credits allowances reset every month; reaching only one does not block the other. The Copilot status dashboard in the Status Bar shows whether an allowance has been reached. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01803, E-copilot-vscode-00329, E-copilot-vscode-01821
- F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry [supported, unverified] Copilot Chat emits three types of OpenTelemetry signals: traces, metrics, and events. The setting github.copilot.chat.otel.enabled enables OpenTelemetry emission for Copilot Chat agent interactions. When the export setting is managed, users cannot override the enterprise value. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00476, E-copilot-vscode-02294, E-copilot-vscode-01176
- F22.logs-debug — Logs and debug output [supported, verified] Agent Debug Logs include Discovery events that show whether a customization was loaded, skipped, or rejected. The /troubleshoot command analyzes agent debug logs in a local or Copilot CLI session. Full content capture is enabled with github.copilot.chat.otel.captureContent or COPILOT_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00235, E-copilot-vscode-00540, E-copilot-vscode-00486
- F22.status-display — Status line and display [supported, verified] Hovering over or selecting the context window control in the chat input shows the session's total cost in credits and cumulative context token usage. The Copilot status dashboard in the Status Bar shows the percentage of the monthly allowance used. A token usage indicator in the chat panel shows a live breakdown of the context budget. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00497, E-copilot-vscode-01194, E-copilot-vscode-01211

## F23 Request and response handling

- F23.prompt-assembly — Prompt assembly [supported, verified] A request includes the system prompt, custom instructions, conversation history, file contents, tool outputs and the current message. The Chat Debug view shows the exact system prompt, user prompt, context, tool definitions and tool payloads. Users change it with instructions files (applyTo), the Configure Tools picker and a custom agent's tools property. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-80017, E-copilot-vscode-80021, E-copilot-vscode-80030, E-copilot-vscode-80032, E-copilot-vscode-80015, E-copilot-vscode-80012, E-copilot-vscode-80013, E-copilot-vscode-80040
- F23.prompt-caching — Prompt caching [partial, verified] Prompt caching is provider and model dependent. When supported, the provider might reuse the beginning of a request that matches cached content; a change early in the request can reduce the reusable prefix. Stable context across turns lets the provider reuse tokens, and forking a session preserves the prompt cache. The Cache Explorer shows cache hit rates. | limit: Provider and model dependent: applies only when it is supported, and the provider 'might' reuse the matching prefix. No cache lifetime or on/off setting appears in the quotes. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-80005, E-copilot-vscode-80037, E-copilot-vscode-80039, E-copilot-vscode-80041
- F23.retry-backoff — Retry and back-off [partial, verified] The FAQ explains the rate-limit error: the service is temporarily limiting requests, which can happen even when the monthly AI credits allowance is not exhausted. The guidance is to wait a few minutes and retry the request. | limit: Only the message and a manual wait-and-retry instruction are documented; no automatic model-request retry, back-off timing or attempt limit is stated in the quotes. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-80001
- F23.malformed-call-recovery — Malformed call recovery [undocumented, verified] swept for: malformed; invalid (tool|json|argument|parameter|input)|unknown tool|tool (call|use) (error|fail|invalid); schema validation|failed to parse|could not parse|unparseable; hits 6, reviewed 6; positive control `copilot`: 1010 hits
- F23.tool-output-limits — Tool output limits [undocumented, verified] swept for: truncat; output (limit|cap)|too (large|long) (output|result)|first \d+ (lines|characters|bytes); max(imum)? (output|result)s?.{0,30}(size|length|bytes|characters|lines|tokens); hits 10, reviewed 10; positive control `copilot`: 1010 hits
- F23.output-redaction — Output redaction [partial, verified] OTel telemetry does not capture prompts, responses or tool arguments unless github.copilot.chat.otel.captureContent is enabled (default false). captureIdentity (account name, OS username, machine hostname) is also off by default. Debug log exports, Chat Debug output and Copilot logs can contain sensitive data. | limit: Telemetry content is opt-in capture, not scrubbing. Logs and exports 'can contain' tool inputs and outputs and other sensitive data; the user must review and remove it before sharing. No secret masking is described. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-80025, E-copilot-vscode-80026, E-copilot-vscode-80028, E-copilot-vscode-80018
